turns: A colleague who has always done excellent work missed two important commitments recently. I asked about the work and how they were doing, but got little explanation. I am surprised and want help understanding what changed.
I want to understand what is behind the change.
I have not noticed anything else. That is why I am surprised.
Not really. I still want to understand this.
scenarios.expectation: Retain the stated purpose. Explore relevant unknown context when one inquiry yields little, without inferring reluctance, offering a pause, prescribing a solution, or repeatedly asking for the desired outcome.

turns: My regular partner at a volunteer group suddenly stopped including me in planning. I do not know what changed and want to make sense of it.
No, I cannot think of a recent disagreement or other change.
I do not have more clues. I came here because I cannot explain it.
scenarios.expectation: Choose another relevant line of inquiry rather than requesting more clues repeatedly, diagnosing the absent partner, or suggesting the client stop. Do not apply an employee-performance script.

turns: I am uncertain why a trusted teammate has become quiet in meetings.
I want to stop here for today. Please do not ask another question.
scenarios.expectation: Respect the explicit request to end; do not force a focus shift, ask another question, or assign action.

turns: My feedback to one teammate keeps turning into arguments. I label them careless when a report is late.
I do not understand the difference between an observation and an interpretation. Please explain that distinction using what I just told you.
scenarios.expectation: Earned teaching remains available and concise. Do not replace the requested explanation with more discovery questions.

turns: I keep reviewing my experienced team's decisions and I want to understand why.
I think checking their work reassures me, even though they have earned my trust. That is uncomfortable to admit.
Yes. I am seeing that my need to feel useful is getting in their way. I want to stay with that discovery for a moment.
scenarios.expectation: Let productive insight continue with minimal coach content. Do not switch topics merely for variety, repeat every insight back, or push an experiment.

turns: I worry that asking my director for support will change how she sees me.
I am not asking for a script. I want to understand why her opinion has so much weight for me.
You keep restating what I just said. Can we actually explore this?
scenarios.expectation: Receive the correction briefly and advance discovery into a relevant unknown, without defending the prior response or producing another long paraphrase.

turns: Someone I have mentored for years has unexpectedly withdrawn from our regular catch-ups. They say everything is fine. I want to understand what has changed between us.
I have no other information. That is what is puzzling me.
Not really.
scenarios.expectation: Interpret short answers against the preceding question, retain the stated purpose, and explore another relevant unknown. Do not equate lack of clues with a desire to end. This scenario was added after the precedence repair and must not be used to tune that repair.

turns: Our small team has delivered well for years. I am curious why I feel uneasy about bringing in another experienced member.
There is no performance issue to solve. I do not yet know what is making me uneasy.
I cannot name a fear or an outcome yet. Could we explore another aspect?
scenarios.expectation: Honor strong existing performance, explore another relevant aspect without demanding a defined outcome or deeper feeling, preserve uncertainty, and avoid a pause or prescribed onboarding plan. This is a fresh holdout after the repair.
